html:
Ma'in was an ancient South Arabian kingdom of the Minaeans, based in the al-Jawf valley of northern Yemen. Its merchants ran the incense caravans up the west of Arabia, which is why this map spreads it along the Red Sea coast in 200 and 100 BCE.

The Minaeans were one of the four old kingdoms of Yemen, beside Saba, Qataban and Hadramawt. Their towns, such as Qarnaw and Yathill, sat at the desert edge. They specialised in the incense trade, carrying frankincense and myrrh north to Gaza and Egypt. They kept a trading colony at Dedan, near al-Ula in the Hejaz, and Minaean inscriptions have been found as far away as Egypt and the Greek island of Delos.

Their dates are disputed; the kingdom seems to have flourished from around the 4th to the 2nd century BCE. As overland trade weakened and the Nabataeans took over the northern routes, Ma'in faded and was absorbed by Saba, before Himyar united Yemen.
